as_told.title: Diane Hennacy Powell's research on autistic telepathy

plain: The Telepathy Tapes is a 2024 podcast series about autistic people who cannot speak. An analyst named Matthew Pines describes it on Jesse Michels's podcast as the story of dozens of such people who are said to share a telepathic link with one caregiver, usually their mother. He credits the work of a doctor named Diane Hennacy Powell. If true, it would mean minds can pass thoughts directly to each other. A scientist, Don Hoffman, says he has seen studies in which an autistic child who can barely control their body reads what is in their mother's mind, and that some of the experiment designs looked fairly rigorous to him. A retired Navy admiral, Tim Gallaudet, also points to Powell's work with autistic patients, framing it as her own research over many years rather than as the podcast. So three separate guests bring it up, each on their own terms.
